CHIEF COMPLAINT
Abnormal lab finding - positive Lyme titer.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Michelle is a 31-year-old female presenting with newly diagnosed Lyme disease. Patient reports a history of an insect bite sustained while hiking in the woods approximately two weeks ago. Since that time, she has developed fatigue, significantly decreased energy levels, and joint pain and swelling in both elbows. She also reports generalized body aches. She notes a bull's-eye rash on her abdomen. Patient has experienced mild nausea and decreased appetite, tolerating only toast and crackers. She denies high fevers. Regarding her diabetes management, she reports that blood sugars have remained relatively stable with occasional mild fluctuations but nothing significantly out of range.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive for fatigue, nausea, decreased appetite, body aches, and bilateral elbow joint pain. Negative for fever, abdominal pain, and diarrhea. Patient confirmed endorsement of nausea and joint pain on review of systems sheet at check-in.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Type 2 diabetes mellitus
Hypertension

MEDICATIONS
Metformin (for diabetes)
Lisinopril 10 mg daily (for hypertension)

ALLERGIES
Not documented in conversation.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented in conversation.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient reports recent hiking in wooded areas. She monitors blood pressure at home using a purchased cuff and reports adhering to a low-sodium diet.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Within normal limits, afebrile.
Cardiovascular and pulmonary: Normal.
Musculoskeletal: Bilateral elbow joint swelling with pain to palpation.
Skin: Bull's-eye rash noted on left-hand side of abdomen, warm to palpation, non-tender, no evidence of cellulitis.
Remainder of examination: Unremarkable.

RESULTS
Lyme titer: Elevated.
Complete metabolic panel and complete blood count: Normal, no elevated white blood cell count.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Newly diagnosed Lyme disease: Start doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for three weeks. Consultation with infectious disease specialist to be arranged. Follow-up appointment scheduled for one week.
2. Type 2 diabetes mellitus: Hemoglobin A1c ordered to assess glycemic control and evaluate need for medication adjustment. Continue current metformin therapy.
3. Hypertension: Currently well-controlled. Continue lisinopril 10 mg daily. Refill ordered. Lipid panel ordered. Patient counseled to continue home blood pressure monitoring and maintain low-sodium diet.
